label: Cost to sequence one human genome
why_it_matters: The steepest sustained cost decline ever recorded in any industry, and the reference case for what a real exponential looks like on a chart. It fell faster than Moore's Law for a decade and the fall was visible in published data throughout — nobody needed inside information to see it.
threshold_question: Reading biology crossed its threshold long ago. The unanswered question is why two decades of collapsing read costs have produced comparatively little investable industry outside diagnostics, and whether that is a lesson about the whole framework.
caveat: NHGRI's series changes methodology partway through and the later figures exclude analysis and interpretation, which now cost more than the sequencing. A curve can keep falling while the total cost of the useful output does not.
data_quality: Verified against NHGRI's published series. Re-check the latest figure before citing in an issue.

label: Lithium-ion battery pack price
why_it_matters: The curve that decided the passenger vehicle question, and the reason the hydrogen car thesis failed. It is the clearest available demonstration that a cost curve competes against a rival curve rather than running in isolation.
threshold_question: Whether the decline continues below roughly $80/kWh, where chemistry rather than manufacturing scale becomes the binding constraint. The answer determines how much of the electricity theme is storage and how much is generation.
caveat: The BNEF survey is a volume-weighted average across chemistries and geographies, so it blends a cheap Chinese LFP pack with an expensive Western NMC one. The average can fall on mix shift alone without any single product getting cheaper.
data_quality: Verified against the BNEF annual survey. Endpoints are survey years, not calendar averages.

label: Crystalline silicon solar module price
why_it_matters: Five decades of an almost unbroken learning rate. It is the longest-running curve in the file and the best evidence that a genuine exponential survives recessions, policy reversals and the bankruptcy of most of its early participants.
threshold_question: Nothing outstanding. This curve is included as a calibration reference rather than as a live candidate — it shows what a mature exponential looks like after the investable phase has passed.
caveat: Module price is a shrinking fraction of installed system cost, so a falling module curve now moves the delivered cost of electricity far less than it did in 2010. A curve can continue and stop mattering.
data_quality: Verified against the Our World in Data series, which compiles Nemet and IRENA. The 1976 figure is a nominal price and is not inflation-adjusted.

label: Cost to place one kilogram in low Earth orbit
why_it_matters: The curve underneath the whole space theme. Its shape matters more than its slope: this is not a smooth exponential but a single discontinuity around 2010-2013 when reuse arrived, with four flat decades before it and roughly a decade of flat since.
threshold_question: Whether Starship produces a second step of the same magnitude. A step function can repeat or it can be a one-off, and the two possibilities have completely different consequences. The annual rate quoted here is an artefact of averaging across a step and should not be extrapolated.
caveat: Published list price is not marginal cost and assumes a fully utilised payload, which almost no mission achieves. The real figure paid per useful kilogram is materially higher and is not disclosed by anyone.
data_quality: Latest figure is derived from published list price divided by stated LEO payload, which is a construction rather than a reported number. The 1981 Shuttle figure is a widely cited estimate with a wide range in the literature. Treat both as order-of-magnitude.

label: Cost to synthesise one base of DNA
why_it_matters: The write side of programmable biology, and the constraint that has held the theme back while the read side collapsed. If this curve steepens, the substrate test for synthetic biology starts to pass in practice rather than in principle.
threshold_question: Whether enzymatic synthesis breaks the current plateau. Phosphoramidite chemistry appears to be near its floor, so continued decline requires a method change rather than scale.
caveat: There is no authoritative published series equivalent to NHGRI's, and quoted prices differ by an order of magnitude between oligo pools and clonal genes. These endpoints are assembled from vendor pricing and should be replaced with a single consistent basis before use.
data_quality: UNVERIFIED — values are indicative and the source is a placeholder. Establish a consistent basis and a citable series before this row informs any decision.

label: Simultaneously recorded electrode channels per implant
why_it_matters: The capability curve for neural interfaces. It is included to show that the framework's unit does not have to be a cost — a capability that rises exponentially is the same signal read from the other side.
threshold_question: Whether channel count is even the binding constraint. It may be that decoding quality, implant longevity or surgical throughput limits the field, in which case this curve rises for years without unlocking anything.
caveat: Channel count is the most quotable specification and therefore the most likely to be optimised for demonstration rather than utility. A device with more channels and a shorter working life is a worse device.
data_quality: UNVERIFIED — endpoints are approximate and drawn from device specifications rather than a compiled series. Replace with a citable source before use.

label: Cost per error-corrected logical qubit
why_it_matters: Would be the curve underneath the quantum candidate, if it could be constructed. Its absence is itself the finding: a theme whose central cost curve cannot be measured is not yet trackable by this system.
threshold_question: Whether a defensible denominator exists at all. Physical qubit counts are published and meaningless; logical qubits are what matter and almost nobody reports them on a consistent basis.
caveat: Deliberately left empty rather than filled with a plausible guess. An unauthored row is honest; a fabricated series would silently corrupt every comparison in this file.
data_quality: UNAUTHORED — no values. Populate only if a consistent public basis emerges.

label: Fully loaded cost per general-purpose robot working hour
why_it_matters: Would be the curve that decides the embodied AI candidate, measured against local loaded labour cost for the same task. The comparison, not the level, is what matters.
threshold_question: Whether any manufacturer will disclose it. Demonstration videos are free; unit economics are not, and the absence of disclosure at this stage is itself informative.
caveat: Must include amortised capital, energy, maintenance, downtime and remote human supervision. A figure that omits teleoperation overhead is measuring a different thing entirely, and most public claims do.
data_quality: UNAUTHORED — no values. This is the single highest-value row to populate when disclosure appears.
